definition.name: top_p

top_p.description: Per-row threshold; stride [1]; frozen to float32(0.9).

definition.reference:
import torch

NUMERICAL_TOLERANCE = 1e-2


def run(probs, top_p):
    # Include the crossing token and every token tied with it.
    ordered = torch.sort(probs, dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True).values
    cumulative = ordered.to(torch.float64).cumsum(dim=-1)
    boundary = torch.searchsorted(
        cumulative, top_p.to(torch.float64).unsqueeze(-1), right=False
    ).clamp_max(probs.shape[-1] - 1)
    cutoff = ordered.gather(-1, boundary)

    retained = torch.where(probs >= cutoff, probs, 0).to(torch.float64)
    return (retained / retained.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)).to(probs.dtype)


def check_outputs(actual, expected):
    if isinstance(actual, (tuple, list)):
        assert len(actual) == 1, "Expected one probability tensor"
        actual = actual[0]
    if isinstance(expected, (tuple, list)):
        assert len(expected) == 1, "Expected one probability tensor"
        expected = expected[0]

    assert torch.isfinite(actual).all(), "Nonfinite probabilities"
    assert (actual >= 0).all(), "Negative probabilities"
    assert torch.equal(actual > 0, expected > 0), "Incorrect Top-p support"
    sums = actual.sum(dim=-1)
    assert torch.allclose(
        sums, torch.ones_like(sums),
        rtol=NUMERICAL_TOLERANCE, atol=NUMERICAL_TOLERANCE,
    ), "Probabilities must sum to one"
